summary: How the household's children grow up (Growth, Teaching, Father read it; GrowthLink and ChildBody are the node side). Growth is by MILESTONES ONLY (user 2026-09-28), not by a real-time age formula: a child moves to the next stage when its `next` requirements are ALL met: the game days spent in the stage, the average care it has had in the stage (0..1), the lessons taken in all, the times it has watched a parent work, the distinct topics it has learnt, and (for the last steps) the core curriculum. Every number is here. The stage lives in the child's record (`stage`, `stage_at`, `care_sum`, `care_n`, `lessons`, `watched`, `topics`, ...): an old record without them is placed by its age once (normalize).

stages.name: Infant
stages.summary: Sits up and crawls once it has had days and enough contentment (BabyLink still carries it until its first steps; a Blender infant is the next art step).

stages.name: Toddler
stages.summary: First steps: walks and follows a parent, watches, cannot work.

stages.name: Child
stages.summary: Carries small things, helps with light chores, learns.

stages.name: Teen
stages.summary: Works light jobs from the job book under a skill cap once the core curriculum is done; learns fast.

stages.name: Adult
stages.summary: A full worker of the household: their own core, everything they learned kept.

shapes.summary: The body shape of a stage (Growth.shape_of / body_look). A baby, toddler and child have the flat, asexual child body (ChildLook.body_for_stage: no breasts, no genital shape, flat pelvis, `sex` fit neutral). A teen keeps that body for `neutral_days` days of the stage, then only a modest change: the `sex` fit `sex_fit` of the way from neutral to its look's own, the bust at most `bust_max`, no genital shape, no body hair, no stubble. Clothed always (the default outfit covers torso and hips). An adult has the look's own body (the parents' inherited bust and build).

care.summary: Care quality is sampled every `sample_min` game minutes of the stage: for a baby its contentment (1 - distress, from BabyCare); from the toddler on 0.6 fed within `meal` hours + 0.4 a parent within `attend_m` and awake. `prior` is the average before any sample.

meal.summary: A child with a body eats from the household store every `hours` game hours (the first kind found).

curriculum.summary: What a parent can teach. `kid` is the survival knowledge id (the child's core gets it as known, taught by the parent) and `skill` the skill that gets the points; `xp` is multiplied by the stage's lesson_mult. `min_stage` and `requires` (topic ids the child must have learnt) gate it; `teacher_skill` is the level the teaching parent needs in `skill`, and the parent's own core must know `kid`. `where`: 'home' (the teach job at the hearth) or 'field' (the parent's real job `job` is the lesson: the child goes along and watches it, and the lesson is given when the job finishes with the child near). `actions` are the player's own survival actions a child can watch. `watch_min` game minutes of watching gives one watch credit. `core`: part of the core curriculum.

growing_up.summary: A teen who has done the core curriculum is taken on as a JUNIOR worker of the household (their own SurvivalCore, the `junior.jobs` switched on, their skills held at `junior.skill_cap`); at adulthood the cap is lifted and every job may be given. The skills and knowledge come from the child's own core (its lessons and watching); `baseline_skill * vigor` is the floor of the working skills.

father.summary: The NPC father (the husband when the player is a woman; Father.decide). A day in blocks; his role in each: provider (works outside), teacher (teaches a child due a lesson, the teach job), protector (keeps home and the family together). `take_along` children of at least that stage go with him on his outside jobs; danger (a live predator within danger_m of the home) keeps everyone home for danger_hold_min game minutes.

player_commands.summary: The player as a parent: E on a child, or the Family section of the household screen.
